entries: *Entry 14:
Muldoon's putting them down. I could not even bring myself to watch it happen. Months of work gone in an instant  and with it, lives I had grown attached to.
*Entry 15:

Sorry, could not bring myself to say anything more last time. They are putting down my Troodons. Monsters. Citing 'dangerous behaviour'. Totally inconsistent. If it is 'dangerous behaviour', then why are the raptors surviving?

Not that I would like to see it happen to the orphan raptors  it is not their fault they grew up without a mother. The Troodons had the same problem. Highly intelligent animals need parental care to develop natural behaviours, or else they end up maladjusted. Instead of giving them guidance, They are destroying them.
*Entry 16:

Euthanasia happening today. I have resolved to find a way to save my children. I wouldn't be able to live with myself if I just stood by and let it happen. If Wu thinks of them as experiments, then I must think of them as family.
*Entry 18:

There is an unused quarantine pen. Perhaps I can move the survivors there when no one is watching. I know it is a risk, but at least they'd have a chance. It may not be freedom, but it is better than extinction at our hands.
*Entry 38:

Triceratops are learning to avoid the veriformans, staying away from the groves where they flourish. They are overturning decades of assumptions about how 'simple' these reptiles were. Far more intelligent and adaptive than Wu gives them credit for.
*Entry 39:

Finally got approval to start the raptor training program. I have been saying for months now that it is absurd to raise these highly intelligent animals without any parental influence. Their borderline psychopathic behaviour makes sense if you think of them as orphans.

I'll take the raptor pups into the behavioural facility when They are a week old and do my best to act as mother to them. Best modern analogue is probably an alligator or an ostrich, soI will try and mimic those maternal behaviours. Hoping the raptors'll grow up to be more placid.
Some dayI will convince them to do the same with the Troodons. If they let me.
*Entry 47:

The Troodons are far more intelligent than we realised before. They are showing complex social interactions  food sharing, role-shifting during hunts, even signs of problem-solving. I continue to observe them whenever I can sneak away. If Hammond saw what I have seen, he'd know They are more than just assets.
*Entry 68:

The longer I am here, the more convinced I am that I can not stay. This isn't what I dreamed of  a lost world where the long-dead animals can roam free and show natural behaviours for the first time in millions of years.
Hammond could have created such a wonder here, but instead he just wants a circus. If I stay, maybe I can change this place from the inside. But every day, it feels more impossible.
*Entry 148:

The female Tyrannosaurus is mature now and being led out to her own paddock. She's absolutely gorgeous, but dim-witted  seems to only respond to movement. Yet she remembers me. When I approached the fence, she leaned closer. She must recognise my scent as her mother. That's something Wu's spreadsheets will never understand.
*Entry 159:

Approached by someone claiming to represent BioSyn, Hammond's main commercial rivals. They suggested I join them in their attempt to build something different  a true sanctuary, where these animals can live free. They claim they need a behavioural specialist.
I said I'd consider it. But can I trust them any more than I trust Hammond? Or would I just be trading one cage for another?
*Entry 172:

One of the trikes is showing really odd behaviour. She keeps repeating the same motions  kicking the dirt, snorting, and waving her horns. Stereotypical behaviour in a creature this size is alarming. Stress? Or something deeper?
*Entry 173:

The trike is now showing colour in her crest. Almost like she's in heat  but that's supposed to be a male trait. Perhaps in these ancient animals it is females that show this signal? Or more likely, Wu tinkered too much in the genetic code again. Poor babies.
*Entry 181:

One of the trikes went down today. Classic signs of poisoning. I suspect the veriformans again  back in Mineboseli, I saw bull elephants showing less dietary bias when in heat. If she really is displaying male behaviour, maybe she's eating indiscriminately. Either way, she paid the price for our interference.
*Entry 193:

BioSyn offered to rescue the Troodons. The quarantine pen was never meant to be permanent, it is too cramped. They say they'll send someone once this storm blows over. If they mean it, maybe this is the only chance the Troodons will ever have to be free.
